# THE FRONTIER FORTY [italic]The biggest songs on the relay this cycle, counted from requests, tape sales and how often Lou hums them off air. Here is the top ten.[/italic]
## THE TOP TEN - [bold]1. Neon Over Titan[/bold], Chroma Sleep. Twelve weeks at number one. The crowd sings it without the band on every live tape. - [bold]2. Mama Was a Pipefitter[/bold], Rosie Ketch. The chorus is a list of pipe sizes. Every miner in the Veil knows them all. - [bold]3. Processor Lullaby[/bold], Rosie Ketch. Recorded in a machine hall. You can hear the dam underneath. - [bold]4. Hypersleep Heart[/bold], Chroma Sleep. Up four places. Up eight on Marisol's profile. - [bold]5. Ninety Days to Payday[/bold], Rosie Ketch. Down two. It was payday. - [bold]6. Relay Delay[/bold], Chroma Sleep. A love song where every line arrives three weeks after the last. - [bold]7. Building Better Worlds[/bold], the Weyland-Yutani Corporate Choir. In at seven. Every Company terminal plays it at start of shift, which counts as a request. - [bold]8. Do You Dream, Joe[/bold], Chroma Sleep. Requested mainly by one listener. - [bold]9. No Letter This Time[/bold], Rosie Ketch. The song people cry to in canteens, back for its third year. - [bold]10. Ten Hours Of Static[/bold], artist unknown. We do not have this record. We have never played it. It is at number ten.
## DROPPED OUT - [bold]The Seegson Jingle[/bold], Seegson Marketing. Off the chart after a listener campaign. Still plays every hour.
